budget_items.topic: Regional stormwater coalition dues vs CEI training
budget_items.what_was_said: The town pays dues to the central Mass regional stormwater coalition, which provides training for any number of staff. This was compared with what CEI would charge for a one-off training.
CEI said its annual BMP inspection line is small relative to the whole MS4 allocation; inspections could later be brought in-house.
Possible funding named included town tax dollars, Chapter 90, stormwater funds to DPW, 319 grants, ARPA and MassWorks. The asset management grant was mentioned as in progress.
Speakers estimated the cost to buy and install a catch basin, excluding piping and engineering.

budget_items.topic: Catch basin cleaning equipment vs outsourcing
budget_items.what_was_said: The task force discussed new equipment or contracting out cleaning; a vac truck and per-basin vendor rates were estimated. Participants said the decision belongs with a new DPW director and the town manager.
figures_as_heard: a hundred dollars a catch basin

budget_items.what_was_said: Street sweeping miles dropped from the prior year. Contracting out sweeping was suggested to cost about as much as basin cleaning.
Money for a preliminary stormwater utility/GIS parcel analysis task must be used by June 30 or it returns to free cash. CEI needs a notice to proceed from the town.
The task force's charge includes establishing estimated cost and an ongoing funding source. A chair said they did not want to open a stormwater tax discussion yet.

decisions.decision: The DPW director will speak to the town's grant/administrative staff (Heather) about authorizing the parcel and structure analysis task before the June 30 deadline.
The proposal to expand the task force from five to seven members was not adopted; the group agreed to continue with liaisons attending unofficially.
The next meeting was set for 19 May.
CEI to return the BMP location data matched to street names; the town will look at training town staff for annual inspections once a new DPW director is in place.
CEI agreed to export its BMP evaluation checklist from GIS and share it with the town.

minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force met with its consultant CEI to review the town's MS4 permit compliance: training, BMP inspections, outfall screening, catch basin cleaning and street sweeping. Members stressed the need for a new DPW director before major planning and flagged a June 30 deadline to use remaining year-four consultant funds. A proposal to expand the task force from five to seven members was discussed and not pursued, and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Stormwater Task Force reviewed the town's MS4 permit compliance with its consultant CEI, covering training, BMP inspections, outfall screening, catch basin cleaning and street sweeping.
A proposal to grow the task force from five to seven members was not adopted; liaisons will keep attending unofficially.
The DPW director will ask town grant staff about authorizing the parcel and structure analysis task before the June 30 deadline.
Unspent year-four consultant money for a stormwater utility and GIS parcel analysis returns to free cash if not used by June 30; CEI needs a notice to proceed.
Catch basin cleaning by new equipment or by contractor was left for a new DPW director and the town manager to decide.

why_it_matters: Stormwater permit work, catch basin cleaning and street sweeping are paid from the town budget, mostly taxes, and the choice between buying equipment and hiring a contractor has not been made.
The task force's charge includes an ongoing funding source for stormwater, but the chair said they did not want to open a stormwater tax discussion yet, so any such proposal is still ahead.
watch_next: Whether the notice to proceed is issued to CEI before the June 30 deadline.
The next meeting, set for 19 May.
